radians.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Converts a quantity specified in degrees into radians, with the formula `degrees * (PI / 180)`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/radians.xhtml)

params.degrees: The quantity, in degrees, to be converted to radians.

degrees.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Converts a quantity specified in radians into degrees, with the formula `radians * (180 / PI)`

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/degrees.xhtml)

params.radians: The quantity, in radians, to be converted to degrees.

sin.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns the trigonometric sine of `angle`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/sin.xhtml)

params.angle: The quantity, in radians, of which to return the sine.

cos.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns the trigonometric cosine of `angle`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/cos.xhtml)

params.angle: The quantity, in radians, of which to return the cosine.

tan.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns the trigonometric tangent of `angle`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/tan.xhtml)

params.angle: The quantity, in radians, of which to return the tangent.

asin.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Arc sine, or inverse sine. Calculates the angle whose sine is `x` and is in the range `[-PI/2, PI/2]`. The result is undefined if `x < -1` or `x > 1`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/asin.xhtml)

params.x: The value whose arc sine to return.

asin.returns: The angle whose trigonometric sine is `x`.

acos.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Arc cosine, or inverse cosine. Calculates the angle whose cosine is `x` and is in the range `[0, PI]`.

The result is undefined if `x < -1` or `x > 1`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/acos.xhtml)

params.x: The value whose arc cosine to return.

acos.returns: The angle whose trigonometric cosine is `x`.

atan.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Calculates the arc tangent given a tangent value of `y/x`.

**Note:** Because of the sign ambiguity, the function cannot determine with certainty in
which quadrant the angle falls only by its tangent value. If you need to know the
quadrant, use atan(vec_type y, vec_type x).

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/atan.xhtml)

params.y_over_x: The fraction whose arc tangent to return.

atan.returns:
The trigonometric arc-tangent of `y_over_x` and is
in the range `[-PI/2, PI/2]`.

atan.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Calculates the arc tangent given a numerator and denominator. The signs of `y` and `x` are used to determine the quadrant that the angle lies in. The result is undefined if `x == 0`.

Equivalent to atan2() in GDScript.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/atan.xhtml)

params.y: The numerator of the fraction whose arc tangent to return.
params.x: The denominator of the fraction whose arc tangent to return.

atan.returns:
The trigonometric arc tangent of `y/x` and is in
the range `[-PI, PI]`.

sinh.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Calculates the hyperbolic sine using `(e^x - e^-x)/2`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/sinh.xhtml)

params.x: The value whose hyperbolic sine to return.

cosh.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Calculates the hyperbolic cosine using `(e^x + e^-x)/2`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/cosh.xhtml)

params.x: The value whose hyperbolic cosine to return.

tanh.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Calculates the hyperbolic tangent using `sinh(x)/cosh(x)`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/tanh.xhtml)

params.x: The value whose hyperbolic tangent to return.

asinh.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Calculates the arc hyperbolic sine of `x`, or the inverse of `sinh`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/asinh.xhtml)

params.x: The value whose arc hyperbolic sine to return.

acosh.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Calculates the arc hyperbolic cosine of `x`, or the non-negative inverse of `cosh`. The result is undefined if `x < 1`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/acosh.xhtml)

params.x: The value whose arc hyperbolic cosine to return.

atanh.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Calculates the arc hyperbolic tangent of `x`, or the inverse of `tanh`. The result is undefined if `abs(x) > 1`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/atanh.xhtml)

params.x: The value whose arc hyperbolic tangent to return.

pow.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Raises `x` to the power of `y`.

The result is undefined if `x < 0`, or if `x == 0` and `y <= 0`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/pow.xhtml)

params.x: The value to be raised to the power `y`.
params.y: The power to which `x` will be raised.

pow.returns: The value of `x` raised to the `y` power.

exp.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Raises `e` to the power of `x`. Also known as the natural exponentiation.

Equivalent to `pow(e, x)`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/exp.xhtml)

params.x: The value to exponentiate.

exp2.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Raises `2` to the power of `x`.

Equivalent to `pow(2.0, x)`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/exp2.xhtml)

params.x: The value of the power to which `2` will be raised.

log.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns the natural logarithm of `x`, i.e. the value `y` which satisfies `x == pow(e, y)`. The result is undefined if `x <= 0`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/log.xhtml)

params.x: The value of which to take the natural logarithm.

log2.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns the base-2 logarithm of `x`, i.e. the value `y` which satisfies `x == pow(2, y)`. The result is undefined if `x <= 0`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/log2.xhtml)

params.x: The value of which to take the base-2 logarithm.

sqrt.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns the square root of `x`. The result is undefined if `x < 0`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/sqrt.xhtml)

params.x: The value of which to take the square root.

inversesqrt.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns the inverse of the square root of `x`, or `1.0 / sqrt(x)`. The result is undefined if `x <= 0`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/inversesqrt.xhtml)

params.x: The value of which to take the inverse of the square root.

inversesqrt.returns: The inverse of the square root of `x`.

abs.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns the absolute value of `x`. Returns `x` if `x` is positive, otherwise returns `-1 * x`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/abs.xhtml)

params.x: The value of which to return the absolute.

sign.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns `-1` if `x < 0`, `0` if `x == 0`, and `1` if `x > 0`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/sign.xhtml)

params.x: The value from which to extract the sign.

floor.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns a value equal to the nearest integer that is less than or equal to `x`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/floor.xhtml)

params.x: The value to floor.

floor.returns: The nearest integer that is less than or equal to `x`.

round.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Rounds `x` to the nearest integer.

**Note:** Rounding of values with a fractional part of `0.5` is implementation-dependent.
This includes the possibility that `round(x)` returns the same value as
`roundEven(x)` for all values of `x`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/round.xhtml)

params.x: The value to round.

roundEven.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Rounds `x` to the nearest integer. A value with a fractional part of `0.5` will always round toward the nearest even integer. For example, both `3.5` and `4.5` will round to `4.0`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/roundEven.xhtml)

params.x: The value to round.

trunc.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Truncates `x`. Returns a value equal to the nearest integer to `x` whose absolute value is not larger than the absolute value of `x`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/trunc.xhtml)

params.x: The value to evaluate.

ceil.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns a value equal to the nearest integer that is greater than or equal to `x`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/ceil.xhtml)

params.x: The value to evaluate.

fract.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns the fractional part of `x`.

This is calculated as `x - floor(x)`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/fract.xhtml)

params.x: The value to evaluate.

mod.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns the value of `x modulo y`. This is also sometimes called the remainder.

This is computed as `x - y * floor(x/y)`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/mod.xhtml)

params.x: The value to evaluate.

modf.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Separates a floating-point value `x` into its integer and fractional parts.

The fractional part of the number is returned from the function. The integer part (as a floating-point quantity) is returned in the output parameter `i`.

:param out i: A variable that receives the integer part of `x`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/modf.xhtml)

params.x: The value to separate.

modf.returns: The fractional part of the number.

min.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns the minimum of two values `a` and `b`.

Returns `b` if `b < a`, otherwise returns `a`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/min.xhtml)

max.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns the maximum of two values `a` and `b`.

It returns `b` if `b > a`, otherwise it returns `a`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/max.xhtml)

clamp.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns the value of `x` constrained to the range `minVal` to `maxVal`.

The returned value is computed as `min(max(x, minVal), maxVal)`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/clamp.xhtml)

params.x: The value to constrain.
params.minVal: The lower end of the range into which to constrain `x`.
params.maxVal: The upper end of the range into which to constrain `x`.

mix.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Performs a linear interpolation between `a` and `b` using `c` to weight between them.

Computed as `a * (1 - c) + b * c`.

Equivalent to lerp() in GDScript.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/mix.xhtml)

params.a: The start of the range in which to interpolate.
params.b: The end of the range in which to interpolate.
params.c: The value to use to interpolate between `a` and `b`.

mix.doc:
Selects either value `a` or value `b` based on the value of `c`. For a component of `c` that is false, the corresponding component of `a` is returned. For a component of `c` that is true, the corresponding component of `b` is returned. Components of `a` and `b` that are not selected are allowed to be invalid floating-point values and will have no effect on the results.

If `a`, `b`, and `c` are vector types the operation is performed component-wise. For example, `mix(vec2(42, 314), vec2(9.8, 6e23), bvec2(true, false)))` will return `vec2(9.8, 314)`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/mix.xhtml)

params.c: The value used to select between `a` and `b`.

fma.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Performs, where possible, a fused multiply-add operation, returning `a * b + c`. In use cases where the return value is eventually consumed by a variable declared as precise:

- `fma()` is considered a single operation, whereas the expression `a * b + c` consumed by a variable declared as precise is considered two operations.

- The precision of `fma()` can differ from the precision of the expression `a * b + c`.

- `fma()` will be computed with the same precision as any other `fma()` consumed by a precise variable, giving invariant results for the same input values of `a`, `b`, and `c`.

Otherwise, in the absence of precise consumption, there are no special constraints on the number of operations or difference in precision between `fma()` and the expression `a * b + c`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/fma.xhtml)

params.a: The first value to be multiplied.
params.b: The second value to be multiplied.
params.c: The value to be added to the result.

step.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Generates a step function by comparing `b` to `a`.

Equivalent to `if (b < a) { return 0.0; } else { return 1.0; }`. For element `i` of the return value, `0.0` is returned if `b[i] < a[i]`, and `1.0` is returned otherwise.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/step.xhtml)

params.a: The location of the edge of the step function.
params.b: The value to be used to generate the step function.

smoothstep.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Performs smooth Hermite interpolation between `0` and `1` when a < c < b. This is useful in cases where a threshold function with a smooth transition is desired.

Smoothstep is equivalent to:

::

vec_type t; t = clamp((c - a) / (b - a), 0.0, 1.0); return t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t);

Results are undefined if `a >= b`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/smoothstep.xhtml)

params.a: The value of the lower edge of the Hermite function.
params.b: The value of the upper edge of the Hermite function.

isnan.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

For each element `i` of the result, returns `true` if `x[i]` is a positive or negative floating-point `NaN` (Not a Number) and `false` otherwise.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/isnan.xhtml)

params.x: The value to test for `NaN`.

isinf.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

For each element i of the result, returns `true` if x[i] is positive or negative floating-point infinity and false otherwise.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/isinf.xhtml)

params.x: The value to test for infinity.

floatBitsToInt.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns the encoding of the floating-point parameters as `int`.

The floating-point bit-level representation is preserved.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/floatBitsToInt.xhtml)

params.x: The value whose floating-point encoding to return.

floatBitsToUint.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Returns the encoding of the floating-point parameters as `uint`.

The floating-point bit-level representation is preserved.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/floatBitsToInt.xhtml)

params.x: The value whose floating-point encoding to return.

intBitsToFloat.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Converts a bit encoding to a floating-point value. Opposite of `floatBitsToInt<shader_func_floatBitsToInt>`

If the encoding of a `NaN` is passed in `x`, it will not signal and the resulting value will be undefined.

If the encoding of a floating-point infinity is passed in parameter `x`, the resulting floating-point value is the corresponding (positive or negative) floating-point infinity.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/intBitsToFloat.xhtml)

params.x: The bit encoding to return as a floating-point value.

uintBitsToFloat.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Converts a bit encoding to a floating-point value. Opposite of `floatBitsToUint<shader_func_floatBitsToUint>`

If the encoding of a `NaN` is passed in `x`, it will not signal and the resulting value will be undefined.

If the encoding of a floating-point infinity is passed in parameter `x`, the resulting floating-point value is the corresponding (positive or negative) floating-point infinity.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/intBitsToFloat.xhtml)

params.x: The bit encoding to return as a floating-point value.

length.doc:
Returns the length of the vector, i.e., `sqrt(x[0] * x[0] + x[1] * x[1] + ... + x[n] * x[n])`

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/length.xhtml)

params.x: The vector

distance.doc:
Returns the distance between the two points `a` and `b`, i.e., `length(b - a);`

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/distance.xhtml)
distance.returns: The scalar distance between the points

dot.doc:
Returns the dot product of two vectors, `a` and `b`, i.e., `a.x * b.x + a.y * b.y + ...`

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/dot.xhtml)

cross.doc:
Returns the cross product of two vectors, i.e.:

```glsl
vec3( a.y * b.z - b.y * a.z,
      a.z * b.x - b.z * a.x,
      a.x * b.y - b.x * a.y)
```

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/cross.xhtml)

normalize.doc:
Returns a vector with the same direction as `x` but with length `1.0`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/normalize.xhtml)

params.x: The vector to normalize.

reflect.doc:
Calculate the reflection direction for an incident vector.

For a given incident vector `I` and surface normal `N` reflect returns the reflection direction calculated as `I - 2.0 * dot(N, I) * N`.

**Note:** `N` should be normalized in order to achieve the desired result.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/reflect.xhtml)

refract.doc:
Calculate the refraction direction for an incident vector.

For a given incident vector `I`, surface normal `N` and ratio of indices of refraction, `eta`, refract returns the refraction vector, `R`.

`R` is calculated as:

```glsl
k = 1.0 - eta * eta * (1.0 - dot(N, I) * dot(N, I));
if (k < 0.0)
    R = genType(0.0);       // or genDType(0.0)
else
    R = eta * I - (eta * dot(N, I) + sqrt(k)) * N;
```

**Note:** The input parameters I and N should be normalized in order to achieve the desired result.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/refract.xhtml)

params.eta: The ratio of indices of refraction.

faceforward.doc:
Returns a vector pointing in the same direction as another.

Orients a vector to point away from a surface as defined by its normal. If `dot(Nref, I) < 0` faceforward returns `N`, otherwise it returns `-N`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/faceforward.xhtml)

matrixCompMult.doc:
Perform a component-wise multiplication of two matrices.

Performs a component-wise multiplication of two matrices, yielding a result matrix where each component, `result[i][j]` is computed as the scalar product of `x[i][j]` and `y[i][j]`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/matrixCompMult.xhtml)

params.x: The first matrix multiplicand.

outerProduct.doc:
Calculate the outer product of a pair of vectors.

Does a linear algebraic matrix multiply `column * row`, yielding a matrix whose number of rows is the number of components in `column` and whose number of columns is the number of components in `row`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/outerProduct.xhtml)

transpose.doc:
Calculate the transpose of a matrix.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/transpose.xhtml)
transpose.returns: A new matrix that is the transpose of the input matrix `m`.

determinant.doc:
Calculate the determinant of a matrix.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/determinant.xhtml)
determinant.returns: The determinant of the input matrix `m`.

inverse.doc:
Calculate the inverse of a matrix.

The values in the returned matrix are undefined if `m` is singular or poorly-conditioned (nearly singular).

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/inverse.xhtml)

params.m: The matrix of which to take the inverse.

inverse.returns: A new matrix which is the inverse of the input matrix `m`.

lessThan.doc:
Performs a component-wise less-than comparison of two vectors.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/lessThan.xhtml)

params.x: The first vector to compare.

lessThan.returns: A boolean vector in which each element `i` is computed as `x[i] < y[i]`.

greaterThan.doc:
Performs a component-wise greater-than comparison of two vectors.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/greaterThan.xhtml)

params.x: The first vector to compare.

greaterThan.returns: A boolean vector in which each element `i` is computed as `x[i] > y[i]`.

lessThanEqual.doc:
Performs a component-wise less-than-or-equal comparison of two vectors.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/lessThanEqual.xhtml)

params.x: The first vector to compare.

lessThanEqual.returns: A boolean vector in which each element `i` is computed as `x[i] <= y[i]`.

greaterThanEqual.doc:
Performs a component-wise greater-than-or-equal comparison of two vectors.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/greaterThanEqual.xhtml)

params.x: The first vector to compare.

greaterThanEqual.returns: A boolean vector in which each element `i` is computed as `x[i] >= y[i]`.

equal.doc:
Performs a component-wise equal-to comparison of two vectors.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/equal.xhtml)

params.x: The first vector to compare.

equal.returns: A boolean vector in which each element `i` is computed as `x[i] == y[i]`.

notEqual.doc:
Performs a component-wise not-equal-to comparison of two vectors.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/notEqual.xhtml)

params.x: The first vector to compare.

notEqual.returns: A boolean vector in which each element `i` is computed as `x[i] != y[i]`.

any.doc:
Returns `true` if any element of a boolean vector is `true`, `false` otherwise.

Functionally equivalent to:

::

bool any(bvec x) {     // bvec can be bvec2, bvec3 or bvec4 bool result = false; int i; for (i = 0; i < x.length(); ++i) { result |= x[i]; } return result; }

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/any.xhtml)

params.x: The vector to be tested for truth.

any.returns: `true` if any element of `x` is `true` and `false` otherwise.

all.doc:
Returns `true` if all elements of a boolean vector are `true`, `false` otherwise.

Functionally equivalent to:

::

bool all(bvec x)       // bvec can be bvec2, bvec3 or bvec4 { bool result = true; int i; for (i = 0; i < x.length(); ++i) { result &= x[i]; } return result; }

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/all.xhtml)

params.x: The vector to be tested for truth.

all.returns: `true` if all elements of `x` are `true` and `false` otherwise.

not.doc:
Logically inverts a boolean vector.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/not.xhtml)

params.x: The vector to be inverted.

not.returns: A boolean vector in which each element `i` is computed as `!x[i]`.

textureSize.doc:
Retrieves the dimensions of a level of a texture.

Returns the dimensions of level `lod` (if present) of the texture bound to sampler.

The components in the return value are filled in, in order, with the width, height and depth of the texture. For the array forms, the last component of the return value is the number of layers in the texture array.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/textureSize.xhtml)

params.s: The sampler to which the texture whose dimensions to retrieve is bound.
params.lod: The level of the texture for which to retrieve the dimensions.

textureSize.returns: The dimensions of level `lod` (if present) of the texture bound to sampler.

textureQueryLod.doc:
**Note:** Available only in the fragment shader.

Compute the level-of-detail that would be used to sample from a texture.

The mipmap array(s) that would be accessed is returned in the x component of the return value. The computed level-of-detail relative to the base level is returned in the y component of the return value.

If called on an incomplete texture, the result of the operation is undefined.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/textureQueryLod.xhtml)

params.s: The sampler to which the texture whose level-of-detail will be queried is bound.
params.p: The texture coordinates at which the level-of-detail will be queried.

textureQueryLevels.doc:
Compute the number of accessible mipmap levels of a texture.

If called on an incomplete texture, or if no texture is associated with sampler, `0` is returned.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/textureQueryLevels.xhtml)

params.s: The sampler to which the texture whose mipmap level count will be queried is bound.

textureQueryLevels.returns: The number of accessible mipmap levels in the texture, or `0`.

texture.doc:
Retrieves texels from a texture.

Samples texels from the texture bound to `s` at texture coordinate `p`. An optional bias, specified in `bias` is included in the level-of-detail computation that is used to choose mipmap(s) from which to sample.

For shadow forms, the last component of `p` is used as Dsub and the array layer is specified in the second to last component of `p`. (The second component of `p` is unused for 1D shadow lookups.)

For non-shadow variants, the array layer comes from the last component of P.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/texture.xhtml)

params.s: The sampler to which the texture from which texels will be retrieved is bound.
params.p: The texture coordinates at which texture will be sampled.
params.bias: An optional bias to be applied during level-of-detail computation.

textureProj.doc:
Performs a texture lookup with projection.

The texture coordinates consumed from `p`, not including the last component of `p`, are divided by the last component of `p`. The resulting 3rd component of `p` in the shadow forms is used as Dref. After these values are computed, the texture lookup proceeds as in texture.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/textureProj.xhtml)

params.s: The sampler to which the texture from which texels will be retrieved is bound.
params.p: The texture coordinates at which texture will be sampled.
params.bias: Optional bias to be applied during level-of-detail computation.

textureLod.doc:
Performs a texture lookup at coordinate `p` from the texture bound to sampler with an explicit level-of-detail as specified in `lod`. `lod` specifies λbase and sets the partial derivatives as follows:

::

δu/δx=0, δv/δx=0, δw/δx=0 δu/δy=0, δv/δy=0, δw/δy=0

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/textureLod.xhtml)

params.s: The sampler to which the texture from which texels will be retrieved is bound.
params.p: The texture coordinates at which texture will be sampled.

textureProjLod.doc:
Performs a texture lookup with projection from an explicitly specified level-of-detail.

The texture coordinates consumed from `p`, not including the last component of `p`, are divided by the last component of `p`. The resulting 3rd component of `p` in the shadow forms is used as Dref. After these values are computed, the texture lookup proceeds as in textureLod, with `lod` used to specify the level-of-detail from which the texture will be sampled.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/textureProjLod.xhtml)

params.s: The sampler to which the texture from which texels will be retrieved is bound.
params.p: The texture coordinates at which texture will be sampled.
params.lod: The explicit level-of-detail from which to fetch texels.

textureGrad.doc:
Performs a texture lookup at coordinate `p` from the texture bound to sampler with explicit texture coordinate gradients as specified in `dPdx` and `dPdy`. Set: - `δs/δx=δp/δx` for a 1D texture, `δp.s/δx` otherwise - `δs/δy=δp/δy` for a 1D texture, `δp.s/δy` otherwise - `δt/δx=0.0` for a 1D texture, `δp.t/δx` otherwise - `δt/δy=0.0` for a 1D texture, `δp.t/δy` otherwise - `δr/δx=0.0` for a 1D or 2D texture, `δp.p/δx` otherwise - `δr/δy=0.0` for a 1D or 2D texture, `δp.p/δy` otherwise

For the cube version, the partial derivatives of `p` are assumed to be in the coordinate system used before texture coordinates are projected onto the appropriate cube face.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/textureGrad.xhtml)

params.s: The sampler to which the texture from which texels will be retrieved is bound.
params.p: The texture coordinates at which texture will be sampled.
params.dPdx: The partial derivative of P with respect to window x.
params.dPdy: The partial derivative of P with respect to window y.

textureProjGrad.doc:
Performs a texture lookup with projection and explicit gradients.

The texture coordinates consumed from `p`, not including the last component of `p`, are divided by the last component of `p`. After these values are computed, the texture lookup proceeds as in textureGrad, passing `dPdx` and `dPdy` as gradients.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/textureProjGrad.xhtml)

params.s: The sampler to which the texture from which texels will be retrieved is bound.
params.p: The texture coordinates at which texture will be sampled.
params.dPdx: The partial derivative of `p` with respect to window x.
params.dPdy: The partial derivative of `p` with respect to window y.

texelFetch.doc:
Performs a lookup of a single texel from texture coordinate `p` in the texture bound to sampler.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/texelFetch.xhtml)

params.s: The sampler to which the texture from which texels will be retrieved is bound.
params.p: The texture coordinates at which texture will be sampled.
params.lod: Specifies the level-of-detail within the texture from which the texel will be fetched.

textureGather.doc:
Gathers four texels from a texture.

Returns the value:

::

vec4(Sample_i0_j1(p, base).comps, Sample_i1_j1(p, base).comps, Sample_i1_j0(p, base).comps, Sample_i0_j0(p, base).comps);

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/textureGather.xhtml)

params.s: The sampler to which the texture from which texels will be retrieved is bound.
params.p: The texture coordinates at which texture will be sampled.
params.comps: *optional* the component of the source texture (0 -> x, 1 -> y, 2 -> z, 3 -> w) that will be used to generate the resulting vector. Zero if not specified.

dFdx.doc:
**Note:** Available only in the fragment shader.

Returns the partial derivative of `p` with respect to the window x coordinate using local differencing.

Returns either dFdxCoarse or dFdxFine. The implementation may choose which calculation to perform based upon factors such as performance or the value of the API `GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER_DERIVATIVE_HINT` hint.

**Warning:** Expressions that imply higher order derivatives such as `dFdx(dFdx(n))`
have undefined results, as do mixed-order derivatives such as `dFdx(dFdy(n))`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/dFdx.xhtml)

params.p:
The expression of which to take the partial derivative.

.. note:: It is assumed that the expression `p` is continuous and therefore expressions evaluated via non-uniform control flow may be undefined.

dFdxCoarse.doc:
**Note:** Available only in the fragment shader.
Not available when using the Compatibility renderer.

Returns the partial derivative of `p` with respect to the window x coordinate.

Calculates derivatives using local differencing based on the value of `p` for the current fragment's neighbors, and will possibly, but not necessarily, include the value for the current fragment. That is, over a given area, the implementation can compute derivatives in fewer unique locations than would be allowed for the corresponding dFdxFine function.

**Warning:** Expressions that imply higher order derivatives such as `dFdx(dFdx(n))`
have undefined results, as do mixed-order derivatives such as `dFdx(dFdy(n))`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/dFdx.xhtml)

params.p:
The expression of which to take the partial derivative.

.. note:: It is assumed that the expression `p` is continuous and therefore
    expressions evaluated via non-uniform control flow may be undefined.

dFdxFine.doc:
**Note:** Available only in the fragment shader.
Not available when using the Compatibility renderer.

Returns the partial derivative of `p` with respect to the window x coordinate.

Calculates derivatives using local differencing based on the value of `p` for the current fragment and its immediate neighbor(s).

**Warning:** Expressions that imply higher order derivatives such as `dFdx(dFdx(n))`
have undefined results, as do mixed-order derivatives such as `dFdx(dFdy(n))`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/dFdx.xhtml)

params.p:
The expression of which to take the partial derivative.

.. note:: It is assumed that the expression `p` is continuous and therefore expressions evaluated via non-uniform control flow may be undefined.

dFdy.doc:
**Note:** Available only in the fragment shader.

Returns the partial derivative of `p` with respect to the window y coordinate using local differencing.

Returns either dFdyCoarse or dFdyFine. The implementation may choose which calculation to perform based upon factors such as performance or the value of the API `GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER_DERIVATIVE_HINT` hint.

**Warning:** Expressions that imply higher order derivatives such as `dFdx(dFdx(n))`
have undefined results, as do mixed-order derivatives such as `dFdx(dFdy(n))`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/dFdx.xhtml)

params.p:
The expression of which to take the partial derivative.

.. note:: It is assumed that the expression `p` is continuous and therefore expressions evaluated via non-uniform control flow may be undefined.

dFdyCoarse.doc:
**Note:** Available only in the fragment shader.
Not available when using the Compatibility renderer.

Returns the partial derivative of `p` with respect to the window y coordinate.

Calculates derivatives using local differencing based on the value of `p` for the current fragment's neighbors, and will possibly, but not necessarily, include the value for the current fragment. That is, over a given area, the implementation can compute derivatives in fewer unique locations than would be allowed for the corresponding dFdyFine and dFdyFine functions.

**Warning:** Expressions that imply higher order derivatives such as `dFdx(dFdx(n))` have undefined results, as do mixed-order derivatives such as `dFdx(dFdy(n))`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/dFdx.xhtml)

params.p:
The expression of which to take the partial derivative.

.. note:: It is assumed that the expression `p` is continuous and therefore expressions evaluated via non-uniform control flow may be undefined.

dFdyFine.doc:
**Note:** Available only in the fragment shader.
Not available when using the Compatibility renderer.

Returns the partial derivative of `p` with respect to the window y coordinate.

Calculates derivatives using local differencing based on the value of `p` for the current fragment and its immediate neighbor(s).

**Warning:** Expressions that imply higher order derivatives such as `dFdx(dFdx(n))` have undefined results, as do mixed-order derivatives such as `dFdx(dFdy(n))`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/dFdx.xhtml)

params.p:
The expression of which to take the partial derivative.

.. note:: It is assumed that the expression `p` is continuous and therefore expressions evaluated via non-uniform control flow may be undefined.

fwidth.doc:
Returns the sum of the absolute value of derivatives in x and y.

Uses local differencing for the input argument `p`.

Equivalent to `abs(dFdx(p)) + abs(dFdy(p))`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/fwidth.xhtml)

params.p: The expression of which to take the partial derivative.

fwidthCoarse.doc:
**Note:** Available only in the fragment shader.
Not available when using the Compatibility renderer.

Returns the sum of the absolute value of derivatives in x and y.

Uses local differencing for the input argument p.

Equivalent to `abs(dFdxCoarse(p)) + abs(dFdyCoarse(p))`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/fwidth.xhtml)

params.p: The expression of which to take the partial derivative.

fwidthFine.doc:
**Note:** Available only in the fragment shader.
Not available when using the Compatibility renderer.

Returns the sum of the absolute value of derivatives in x and y.

Uses local differencing for the input argument p.

Equivalent to `abs(dFdxFine(p)) + abs(dFdyFine(p))`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/fwidth.xhtml)

params.p: The expression of which to take the partial derivative.

packHalf2x16.doc:
Converts two 32-bit floating-point quantities to 16-bit floating-point quantities and packs them into a single 32-bit integer.

Returns an unsigned integer obtained by converting the components of a two-component floating-point vector to the 16-bit floating-point representation found in the OpenGL Specification, and then packing these two 16-bit integers into a 32-bit unsigned integer. The first vector component specifies the 16 least-significant bits of the result; the second component specifies the 16 most-significant bits.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/packHalf2x16.xhtml)

params.v: A vector of two 32-bit floating-point values that are to be converted to 16-bit representation and packed into the result.

unpackHalf2x16.doc:
Inverse of packHalf2x16.

Unpacks a 32-bit integer into two 16-bit floating-point values, converts them to 32-bit floating-point values, and puts them into a vector. The first component of the vector is obtained from the 16 least-significant bits of `v`; the second component is obtained from the 16 most-significant bits of `v`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/unpackHalf2x16.xhtml)

params.v: A single 32-bit unsigned integer containing 2 packed 16-bit floating-point values.

packUnorm2x16.doc:
Pack floating-point values into an unsigned integer.

Converts each component of the normalized floating-point value v into 16-bit integer values and then packs the results into a 32-bit unsigned integer.

The conversion for component c of `v` to fixed-point is performed as follows:

::

round(clamp(c, 0.0, 1.0) * 65535.0)

The first component of the vector will be written to the least significant bits of the output; the last component will be written to the most significant bits.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/packUnorm.xhtml)

params.v: A vector of values to be packed into an unsigned integer.

packUnorm2x16.returns: Unsigned 32 bit integer containing the packed encoding of the vector.

unpackUnorm2x16.doc:
Unpack floating-point values from an unsigned integer.

Unpack single 32-bit unsigned integers into a pair of 16-bit unsigned integers. Then, each component is converted to a normalized floating-point value to generate the returned two-component vector.

The conversion for unpacked fixed point value f to floating-point is performed as follows:

f / 65535.0

The first component of the returned vector will be extracted from the least significant bits of the input; the last component will be extracted from the most significant bits.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/unpackUnorm.xhtml)

params.v: An unsigned integer containing packed floating-point values.

packSnorm2x16.doc:
Packs floating-point values into an unsigned integer.

Convert each component of the normalized floating-point value `v` into 16-bit integer values and then packs the results into a 32-bit unsigned integer.

The conversion for component c of `v` to fixed-point is performed as follows:

::

round(clamp(c, -1.0, 1.0) * 32767.0)

The first component of the vector will be written to the least significant bits of the output; the last component will be written to the most significant bits.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/packUnorm.xhtml)

params.v: A vector of values to be packed into an unsigned integer.

packSnorm2x16.returns: Unsigned 32 bit integer containing the packed encoding of the vector.

unpackSnorm2x16.doc:
Unpacks floating-point values from an unsigned integer.

Unpacks single 32-bit unsigned integers into a pair of 16-bit signed integers. Then, each component is converted to a normalized floating-point value to generate the returned two-component vector.

The conversion for unpacked fixed point value f to floating-point is performed as follows:

clamp(f / 32727.0, -1.0, 1.0)

The first component of the returned vector will be extracted from the least significant bits of the input; the last component will be extracted from the most significant bits.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/unpackUnorm.xhtml)

params.v: An unsigned integer containing packed floating-point values.

packUnorm4x8.doc:
Packs floating-point values into an unsigned integer.

Converts each component of the normalized floating-point value `v` into 16-bit integer values and then packs the results into a 32-bit unsigned integer.

The conversion for component c of `v` to fixed-point is performed as follows:

::

round(clamp(c, 0.0, 1.0) * 255.0)

The first component of the vector will be written to the least significant bits of the output; the last component will be written to the most significant bits.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/packUnorm.xhtml)

params.v: A vector of values to be packed into an unsigned integer.

packUnorm4x8.returns: Unsigned 32 bit integer containing the packed encoding of the vector.

unpackUnorm4x8.doc:
Unpacks floating-point values from an unsigned integer.

Unpacks single 32-bit unsigned integers into four 8-bit unsigned integers. Then, each component is converted to a normalized floating-point value to generate the returned four-component vector.

The conversion for unpacked fixed point value f to floating-point is performed as follows:

f / 255.0

The first component of the returned vector will be extracted from the least significant bits of the input; the last component will be extracted from the most significant bits.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/unpackUnorm.xhtml)

params.v: An unsigned integer containing packed floating-point values.

packSnorm4x8.doc:
Packs floating-point values into an unsigned integer.

Convert each component of the normalized floating-point value `v` into 16-bit integer values and then packs the results into a 32-bit unsigned integer.

The conversion for component c of `v` to fixed-point is performed as follows:

::

round(clamp(c, -1.0, 1.0) * 127.0)

The first component of the vector will be written to the least significant bits of the output; the last component will be written to the most significant bits.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/packUnorm.xhtml)

params.v: A vector of values to be packed into an unsigned integer.

packSnorm4x8.returns: Unsigned 32 bit integer containing the packed encoding of the vector.

unpackSnorm4x8.doc:
Unpack floating-point values from an unsigned integer.

Unpack single 32-bit unsigned integers into four 8-bit signed integers. Then, each component is converted to a normalized floating-point value to generate the returned four-component vector.

The conversion for unpacked fixed point value f to floating-point is performed as follows:

clamp(f / 127.0, -1.0, 1.0)

The first component of the returned vector will be extracted from the least significant bits of the input; the last component will be extracted from the most significant bits.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/unpackUnorm.xhtml)

params.v: An unsigned integer containing packed floating-point values.

bitfieldExtract.doc:
Extracts a subset of the bits of `value` and returns it in the least significant bits of the result. The range of bits extracted is `[offset, offset + bits - 1]`.

The most significant bits of the result will be set to zero.

**Note:** If bits is zero, the result will be zero.

**Warning:** The result will be undefined if:

- offset or bits is negative.
- if the sum of offset and bits is greater than the number of bits used to store the operand.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/bitfieldExtract.xhtml)

params.value: The integer from which to extract bits.
params.offset: The index of the first bit to extract.
params.bits: The number of bits to extract.

bitfieldExtract.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Extracts a subset of the bits of `value` and returns it in the least significant bits of the result. The range of bits extracted is `[offset, offset + bits - 1]`.

The most significant bits will be set to the value of `offset + base - 1` (i.e., it is sign extended to the width of the return type).

**Note:** If bits is zero, the result will be zero.

**Warning:** The result will be undefined if:

- offset or bits is negative.
- if the sum of offset and bits is greater than the number of bits used to store the operand.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/bitfieldExtract.xhtml)

params.value: The integer from which to extract bits.
params.offset: The index of the first bit to extract.
params.bits: The number of bits to extract.

bitfieldExtract.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Inserts the `bits` least significant bits of `insert` into `base` at offset `offset`.

The returned value will have bits [offset, offset + bits + 1] taken from [0, bits - 1] of `insert` and all other bits taken directly from the corresponding bits of base.

**Note:** If bits is zero, the result will be the original value of base.

**Warning:** The result will be undefined if:

- offset or bits is negative.
- if the sum of offset and bits is greater than the number of bits used to store the operand.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/bitfieldInsert.xhtml)

params.base: The integer into which to insert `insert`.
params.insert: The value of the bits to insert.
params.offset: The index of the first bit to insert.
params.bits: The number of bits to insert.

bitfieldInsert.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Inserts the `bits` least significant bits of `insert` into `base` at offset `offset`.

The returned value will have bits [offset, offset + bits + 1] taken from [0, bits - 1] of `insert` and all other bits taken directly from the corresponding bits of base.

**Note:** If bits is zero, the result will be the original value of base.

**Warning:** The result will be undefined if:

- offset or bits is negative.
- if the sum of offset and bits is greater than the number of bits used to store the operand.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/bitfieldInsert.xhtml)

params.base: The integer into which to insert `insert`.
params.insert: The value of the bits to insert.
params.offset: The index of the first bit to insert.
params.bits: The number of bits to insert.

bitfieldReverse.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Reverse the order of bits in an integer.

The bit numbered `n` will be taken from bit `(bits - 1) - n` of `value`, where bits is the total number of bits used to represent `value`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/bitfieldReverse.xhtml)

params.value: The value whose bits to reverse.

bitCount.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Counts the number of 1 bits in an integer.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/bitCount.xhtml)

params.value: The value whose bits to count.

bitCount.returns: The number of bits that are set to 1 in the binary representation of `value`.

findLSB.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Find the index of the least significant bit set to `1`.

**Note:** If `value` is zero, `-1` will be returned.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/findLSB.xhtml)

params.value: The value whose bits to scan.

findLSB.returns: The bit number of the least significant bit that is set to 1 in the binary representation of value.

findMSB.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Find the index of the most significant bit set to 1.

**Note:** For signed integer types, the sign bit is checked first and then:
 - For positive integers, the result will be the bit number of the most significant bit that is set to 1.
 - For negative integers, the result will be the bit number of the most significant bit set to 0.

**Note:** For a value of zero or negative 1, -1 will be returned.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/findMSB.xhtml)

params.value: The value whose bits to scan.

findMSB.returns: The bit number of the most significant bit that is set to 1 in the binary representation of value.

imulExtended.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Perform 32-bit by 32-bit signed multiplication to produce a 64-bit result.

The 32 least significant bits of this product are returned in `lsb` and the 32 most significant bits are returned in `msb`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/umulExtended.xhtml)

params.x: The first multiplicand.
params.msb: The variable to receive the most significant word of the product.
params.lsb: The variable to receive the least significant word of the product.

umulExtended.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Perform 32-bit by 32-bit unsigned multiplication to produce a 64-bit result.

The 32 least significant bits of this product are returned in `lsb` and the 32 most significant bits are returned in `msb`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/umulExtended.xhtml)

params.x: The first multiplicand.
params.msb: The variable to receive the most significant word of the product.
params.lsb: The variable to receive the least significant word of the product.

uaddCarry.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Adds two 32-bit unsigned integer values (scalars or vectors) and returns a 32-bit unsigned integer, along with a carry output stored in `carry`.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/uaddCarry.xhtml)

params.x: The first operand.
params.carry: `0` if the sum is less than 2^32, otherwise `1`.

usubBorrow.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Subtract unsigned integers and generate borrow.

[OpenGL reference page](https://www.khronos.org/registry/OpenGL-Refpages/gl4/html/usubBorrow.xhtml)

params.x: The first operand.

usubBorrow.returns: The difference of `x` and `y` if non-negative, or 2^32 plus that difference otherwise.

ldexp.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Assembles a floating-point number from a value and exponent.

**Warning:** If this product is too large to be represented in the floating-point
type, the result is undefined.

frexp.doc:
*Component-wise function.*

Extracts `x` into a floating-point significand in the range `[0.5, 1.0)` and in integral exponent of two, such that:

::

x = significand * 2 ^ exponent

For a floating-point value of `0.0`, the significand and exponent are both `0.0`.

**Warning:** For a floating-point value that is an infinity or a floating-point `NaN`, the results are undefined.

spatial.depth_test_inverted: Depth test will discard the pixel if it is in front of other pixels. Useful for stencil effects.
spatial.sss_mode_skin: Subsurface Scattering mode for skin (optimizes visuals for human skin, e.g. boosted red channel).
spatial.unshaded: Result is just albedo. No lighting/shading happens in material, making it faster to render.
spatial.wireframe: Geometry draws using lines (useful for troubleshooting). When using the Compatibility renderer, you must call `RenderingServer.set_debug_generate_wireframes(true)` *before* the mesh is loaded for wireframe rendering to work. In the Compatibility renderer, backface culling is always disabled in wireframe mode, while in the Forward+ and Mobile renderers, the cull mode is respected.
spatial.debug_shadow_splits: Directional shadows are drawn using different colors for each split (useful for troubleshooting).
spatial.specular_schlick_ggx: Schlick-GGX for direct light specular lobes (default).
spatial.specular_toon: Toon for direct light specular lobes.
spatial.specular_disabled: Disable direct light specular lobes. Doesn't affect reflected light (use `SPECULAR = 0.0` instead).
spatial.skip_vertex_transform: `VERTEX`, `NORMAL`, `TANGENT`, and `BITANGENT` need to be transformed manually in the `vertex()` function.
spatial.world_vertex_coords: `VERTEX`, `NORMAL`, `TANGENT`, and `BITANGENT` are modified in world space instead of model space.
spatial.ensure_correct_normals: Use when non-uniform scale is applied to mesh *(note: currently unimplemented)*.
spatial.shadows_disabled: Disable computing shadows in shader. The shader will not receive shadows, but can still cast them.
spatial.ambient_light_disabled: Disable contribution from ambient light and radiance map.
spatial.shadow_to_opacity: Lighting modifies the alpha so shadowed areas are opaque and non-shadowed areas are transparent. Useful for overlaying shadows onto a camera feed in AR.
spatial.vertex_lighting: Use vertex-based lighting instead of per-pixel lighting.
spatial.particle_trails: Enables the trails when used on particle geometry.
spatial.alpha_to_coverage: Alpha antialiasing mode, see [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/40364) for more.
spatial.alpha_to_coverage_and_one: Alpha antialiasing mode, see [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/40364) for more.
spatial.fog_disabled: Disable receiving depth-based or volumetric fog. Useful for `blend_add` materials like particles.

canvas_item.blend_mix: Mix blend mode (alpha is transparency), default.
canvas_item.blend_disabled: Disable blending, values (including alpha) are written as-is.
canvas_item.unshaded: Result is just albedo. No lighting/shading happens in material.
canvas_item.light_only: Only draw in the light pass.
canvas_item.skip_vertex_transform: `VERTEX` needs to be transformed manually in the `vertex()` function.
canvas_item.world_vertex_coords: `VERTEX` is modified in world coordinates instead of local.

particles.keep_data: Do not clear previous data on restart.
particles.collision_use_scale: Scale the particle's size for collisions.

sky.use_half_res_pass: Allows the shader to write to and access the half resolution pass.
sky.use_quarter_res_pass: Allows the shader to write to and access the quarter resolution pass.
sky.disable_fog: If used, fog will not affect the sky.

texture_blit.blend_disabled: Disable blending, values (including alpha) are written as-is. Default.

spatial.write: Write reference value to the stencil buffer.
spatial.write_if_depth_fail: Write reference value to the stencil buffer if the depth test fails.
spatial.compare_equal: Pass stencil test if the reference value is equal to the stencil buffer value.
spatial.compare_not_equal: Pass stencil test if the reference value is not equal to the stencil buffer value.
spatial.compare_less: Pass stencil test if the reference value is less than the stencil buffer value.
spatial.compare_less_or_equal: Pass stencil test if the reference value is less than or equal to the stencil buffer value.
spatial.compare_greater: Pass stencil test if the reference value is greater than the stencil buffer value.
spatial.compare_greater_or_equal: Pass stencil test if the reference value is greater than or equal to the stencil buffer value.

types.void: Void datatype, useful only for functions that return nothing.
types.bool: Boolean datatype, can only contain `true` or `false`.
types.uint: Unsigned scalar integer; can't contain negative numbers.
types.sampler2D: Sampler type for binding 2D textures, which are read as float.
types.isampler2D: Sampler type for binding 2D textures, which are read as signed integer.
types.usampler2D: Sampler type for binding 2D textures, which are read as unsigned integer.
types.sampler2DArray: Sampler type for binding 2D texture arrays, which are read as float.

types.usampler2DArray: Sampler type for binding 2D texture arrays, which are read as unsigned integer.
types.sampler3D: Sampler type for binding 3D textures, which are read as float.

types.usampler3D: Sampler type for binding 3D textures, which are read as unsigned integer.
types.samplerCube: Sampler type for binding Cubemaps, which are read as float.
